newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: France alone blocks Annan for U.N. top post.
newsitem.headline: France alone blocks Annan for U.N. top post.

text.p: All Security Council members except France voted for Kofi Annan, the U.N. undersecretary-general for peacekeeping, for the post of U.N. secretary-general in a straw poll on Thursday, dipliomats said.
They said Annan received a 14-1 vote, which meant France, a veto-bearing permanent council member, was still blocking him. At the close of unofficial balloting on Wednesday Annan had 11 votes.

Annan's nearest rival, Ivory Coast Foreign Minister Amara Essy, received seven votes in the second of two polls taken on Thursday, with two permanent members of the council, presumed to be the United States and Britain, casting negative votes, the envoys said.

To be elected, a candidate must have a minimum of nine votes and no veto from one of the council's five permanent members -- the United States, France, Britain, Russia and China. A negative vote from France, when official balloting begins, would doom Annan's candidacy.

No formal vote has been held since Washington vetoed a second term for Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Nov. 19 while the other 14 council members supported him. His five-year term expires on December 31.
Council President Paolo Fulci said that no new candidates had officially entered the race.
